## Added

- Start UsageDeck automatically when you sign in to Windows, launching quietly in the notification area without opening the full app.
- Pause notifications for 30 minutes, 1 hour, 2 hours, 4 hours, or until the following morning from the tray or **Settings → Notifications**. UsageDeck keeps refreshing in the background, and notifications can be resumed at any time.

## Improvements

- Keep the provider you are viewing current automatically, or select **All providers** to refresh everything together. Refresh requests made while an update is running are queued instead of ignored, and providers are less likely to get stuck when their tools stop responding.
- Recover from unreadable saved settings by restoring the defaults, explaining what happened, and keeping a copy of the old settings when possible.
- Receive sign-in alerts after the first failed update and a recovery alert when the provider reconnects. Turning off provider status also stops further status alerts.
- Find automatic refresh, provider-status monitoring, and start-at-sign-in controls together under **Settings → General → Background activity**.

## Fixes

- OpenAI Codex usage loads with Codex CLI 0.149.0, and switching from GitHub Copilot back to OpenAI Codex no longer closes UsageDeck.
- The tray icon and its menu respond immediately after UsageDeck starts with Windows, including opening the app with a single click.
- The Rate limits section no longer leaves a large empty gap when there are no warnings to show.
- Update notifications in the footer stay within the available space instead of pushing the provider status control out of view.
